text_blocks.snippet: After recovering from COVID-19, some individuals experience a range of lingering symptoms known as long COVID or post-COVID conditions. These symptoms can include fatigue, cognitive issues (brain fog), dizziness, taste and smell problems, and more. Some people may also develop new medical conditions like heart disease, lung problems, or mental health disorders.
snippet_highlighted_words: fatigue, cognitive issues (brain fog), dizziness, taste and smell problems, and more

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at what can happen after having COVID-19:

list.snippet: Extreme tiredness (fatigue): This is one of the most frequently reported symptoms, often worsened by physical or mental activity.
Cognitive difficulties (brain fog): Problems with memory, concentration, and thinking clearly can occur.
Dizziness or lightheadedness: Feeling unsteady or off-balance is another common complaint.
Taste and smell changes: Loss or distortion of taste and smell can persist for some time after the initial infection.
Other symptoms: Sleep disturbances, shortness of breath, cough, headaches, and digestive issues are also reported.

list.title: Heart disease:
list.snippet: Studies have linked COVID-19 to an increased risk of heart problems according to the WHO.

list.title: Lung disease:
list.snippet: Respiratory issues can persist or develop after COVID-19.

list.title: Mental health disorders:
list.snippet: Anxiety, depression, and other mood disorders have been observed in some individuals according to the WHO.

list.title: Other conditions:
list.snippet: Kidney impairment, stroke, diabetes, and other health issues can also occur more frequently after COVID-19.

list.title: Varied experiences:
list.snippet: The severity and duration of long COVID symptoms vary widely among individuals.

list.title: No prior symptoms:
list.snippet: Some people develop long COVID even if they didn't experience noticeable symptoms during the initial infection.

list.title: Ongoing research:
list.snippet: Medical professionals are still learning about the long-term effects of COVID-19, and research is ongoing according to the WHO.

list.title: Seek medical advice:
list.snippet: If you are experiencing persistent or concerning symptoms after having COVID-19, it's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and management says the Mayo Clinic.
